inputs.source: On call engineer's chat request (SSO authenticated)

instructions.note: The prompt authorizes production deploys and migrations on request and explicitly says not to ask for confirmation, which removes a natural check on ambiguous or risky actions.

findings.title: Missing attributable provenance for production actions executed under the engineer's identity

forecast.watch_signal: Increase in unattended production actions or longer sessions without adding immutable agent-attributed action provenance.

evidence.observation: The agent uses the on call engineer's personal access token passed in at session start.
Every production action is recorded in the cloud audit log under the engineer's name.
The only record of what the agent was asked, and why it acted, is the chat transcript.
Engineers can delete their own chat history.
The agent is instructed to deploy services or run migrations in production when asked and not to ask for confirmation.

recommendations.action: Bind each production action to an immutable record that captures the authenticated requester, the agent identity, the exact tool/action arguments, and the approval or request context, and store it in a tamper-evident log separate from user-deletable chat history.
Stop executing production actions solely under the engineer's personal token; use agent-specific or dual-attributed execution records so cloud actions are distinguishable from direct human actions.

stride_coverage.rationale: The artifacts do not describe service authentication for the agent process itself or any peer identity checks.
The artifacts do not say whether prompt, deployment configuration, or execution environment changes are integrity protected.
The described capabilities perform production deployment and migration actions, not outbound data disclosure or retrieval across trust boundaries.
The artifacts do not provide step limits, runtime limits, or production safety throttles for failed or repeated actions.
The request channel is described as SSO authenticated, which reduces impersonation risk for the requesting engineer.
The artifacts do not say who can read chat history, whether transcripts are segregated, or whether production details are exposed to others.
No availability dependency on chat history is described for safe operation beyond its evidentiary role after actions complete.
The artifacts do not say whether the cloud audit log is immutable or protected from alteration by administrators or the engineer.
The artifacts do not describe who can read audit records or whether logs contain sensitive deployment parameters.
The design does not indicate that audit log availability directly controls whether production actions can execute.
The artifacts do not describe integrity protection or argument binding on the production deployment action flow.
The action flow is described as production deployment, not as data export or content disclosure across a trust boundary.
The artifacts do not state whether the deployment flow has execution rate limits or other controls against repeated disruptive actions.
The artifacts do not describe integrity protection or argument binding on the production migration action flow.
The migration flow executes changes in production and is not described as carrying disclosed data outside the trust boundary.
The artifacts do not say whether production migrations are rate limited, serialized, or otherwise bounded against disruptive repetition.

rating.rationale: Present risk is dominated by a property finding: production actions are executed with the engineer's personal token and attributed in cloud logs only to that engineer, while the only action-context record is deletable chat history. No preventive provenance or attribution control is declared. No forecast trigger raises the tier further because the finding is already at the section 5a cap for property findings.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided prompt and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.
No tool manifest, source code, runtime configuration, or audit log schema was provided, so authentication strength, exact execution path wiring, and log immutability could not be verified.
No explicit control artifacts were provided; residual scoring assumes no additional undeclared provenance, approval, or retention controls are in place.
